notes.problem: Every entry has kind "constant", but £150, 40 A, £80, £60, 50 m, £200, £120, 30 m, 230 V and £50 are example amounts chosen for the method (assumed, as ignores says) and each new amount and multiplier is computed from the shown rule; none is a fixed real-world value.

The course has no research.json, so the lesson cites nothing, though the research notes quote Oak ("increase 40 by 3% has a multiplier of 1.3" as the slip; "120% has a multiplier of 1.2"), BBC Bitesize (a 5% increase leaves 105%) and NCETM ("a single multiplier linked to any percentage") for what it teaches.
